What's new

Version 60 · Researched suspension on every car

Suspension

  • All 541 real trims now have their real suspension hardware, researched: MacPherson strut, double wishbone or multi-link, torsion beam or solid axles on leaf springs, coils or air; passive, frequency-selective, adaptive or MagneRide dampers, Multimatic DSSV, Fox internal-bypass and remote-reservoir off-road shocks; front sway-bar disconnects and active anti-roll. Settings › Car shows each car's real setup.
  • Springs now come from each car's real ride feel and weight, instead of the same springs on every car (which made heavy trucks wallow): plush luxury cars around 1.1 Hz, sports cars around 1.7 Hz, and leaf-sprung truck rears stiffer.
  • Solid axles carry their real extra weight, leaf springs have their interleaf friction, and wheel travel matches the real car: a Raptor or TRX can soak up far more than a Camry before hitting the bump stops.
  • Body lean is set from the real car's character. In testing at about 0.5 g: Camry about 3°/g, Q5 about 4.5°/g, Escalade about 6°/g, Gladiator Rubicon about 7°/g, and the RS Q8 with active anti-roll stays almost flat. Sport modes stiffen it a little.
  • Off-road shocks behave like the real ones: Fox bypass shocks firm up deep in their travel, DSSV spool valves stay controlled on big hits, and frequency-selective dampers soften over sharp bumps. MagneRide and fully active systems hold the body flatter.
  • On Gladiator and Wrangler Rubicon, Bronco, Tacoma TRD Off-Road, GX Overtrail and Power Wagon, the front sway bar disconnects by itself in an off-road or terrain mode below 20 mph.
  • Air suspension stays within the car's real ride-height range, and air springs level the car when it's loaded.
  • Traffic cars use the same researched springs and lean.

Version 59 · Real drive modes on every car, and an EV mode box

Drive modes

  • Every real car now has its own drive mode names in the mode box: 541 trims, up from 107. For example the Ranger Raptor has Normal, Sport, Slippery, Sand, Rock Crawl, Mud/Ruts and Baja, the Bronco Sport Badlands adds Rock Crawl and Rally, GM trucks have Tour, Sport, Off-Road, Snow/Ice, Tow/Haul and Terrain, and Hondas have Normal, Econ, Sport and Snow. Cars that really have no mode selector (Chevy Trax, Ram ProMaster) show just Normal.
  • Each mode works the way its type should: Eco softens the throttle, Sport sharpens it and firms up the suspension, Snow and Slippery start gently, the off-road modes let the traction control allow more wheelspin, and Tow/Haul holds gears.
  • The 2019 RAV4's Multi-Terrain Select dial has its real names (Mud & Sand, Rock & Dirt, Snow). Long mode names shrink to fit the box.

EV mode box

  • Hybrids and plug-in hybrids have a new square EV box above the drive mode box, with the car's own name for it.
  • Hybrids: tap for electric only at low speed (it lights green when on). Hybrids that really have no EV button, like the 2025 Camry, don't get one.
  • Plug-in hybrids: tap to step through the car's real battery modes, such as Auto EV, EV Now, EV Later and EV Charge on Fords, Hybrid, Electric and eSave on the Jeep 4xe, or Hybrid, Pure, Hold and Charge on Volvos. EV Now drives on electricity only, EV Later and Hold keep the battery for later, and Charge runs the engine to charge the battery to 80 %.
  • On phones the key, phone and Bluetooth buttons move up to make room.

Version 58 · Faster on slow laptops, proving ground and hills polished

Speed (Surface Go and other slow laptops)

  • The scenery is now split into tiles, and only the tiles in front of you and within sight are drawn. In town that cuts what the graphics chip draws each frame by about two thirds (1.5 million triangles down to about 0.5 million). The proving ground is no longer drawn when you're across town.
  • New Lowest graphics: half resolution, very few cars, shorter view distance, 30 fps. Auto now drops to it by itself if Low still lags.
  • New Frame rate setting (Settings › Graphics): Auto, 30, 60 or Unlimited. 30 fps keeps a Surface Go steadier and cooler, especially while it's charging and running hot.
  • Charging spots and fuel pumps are looked up once instead of hundreds of times a second while you charge.

Proving ground

  • Every section board has its name and what it tests written on it, on a bigger board on two posts.
  • The 10 %, 20 % and 30 % hills now have real vertical curves: the slope eases in and out at the bottom and top instead of a sharp kink.
  • The hills have solid sides and guard rails along both edges, so you can't drive off the top. The rails, sign posts and other proving ground obstacles now really block you; they were being wiped from the collision list before.

Hills

  • Grass no longer pokes through any road: every road nearby now pulls the ground down under it, not just the nearest one. A check of 71,000 points along every road found none left (15 before).

Version 57 · Park assist everywhere

Park assist

  • Park assist now works on the garage ramps. It used to creep too weakly on the slope, stop and roll backwards. Its speed control now measures which way you're really rolling, adds the extra throttle a slope needs, and holds the brake while it does, so it parks smoothly uphill and downhill on every level.
  • Store charging stations have painted bays, and park assist backs you into them, lined up with the charger.
  • Tested on every kind of space: both garage bays (uphill and downhill, ground and upper levels), the store parking lots, Main St parallel parking, the charger plaza and store charging bays. It finished every one with no hits, centred in the space and less than 1.5° off straight.

Fixes

  • Building a new car while you're on an upper level of the garage no longer drops it to the ground floor.

Version 56 · New 2-bay double-threaded helix garage

Parking garage

  • The Fort St garage is rebuilt as a real 2-bay double-threaded helix. There are no flat decks: every floor is a gentle ramp (1 in 15) and you park right on the slope.
  • The north bay climbs a full level going east, the south bay a full level going west, with flat turn landings at both ends. The two threads wind round each other a level apart and each one climbs two levels per lap.
  • Two entrances off Fort St, each with its own ticket and pay gates: the west entrance takes you up one thread, the east entrance up the other. Four levels of ramps up to an open roof.
  • Stall lines on both sides of every aisle, a centre wall between the bays, columns, parapets, lights under every slab, and a coloured band on each landing. Parked cars sit level across the slope, and park assist finds stalls on the ramp you're on.

Version 55 · Car builder: your money, a new start button, stay where you are

Car builder

  • Your money is shown at the top of the builder (green), and under the price as "You have $…". It turns amber when the car costs more than you have.
  • The Start test drive button is now a glowing orange button with a steering wheel, so it stands out from the Next buttons.
  • Building a new car out on the map (Redo car or Spawn another car) no longer sends you back to the start. You come out right where you were. If your old car is parked there, the new one appears just ahead of it.

Version 54 · Cleaner settings, sharper traffic lights

Settings

  • Settings has a cleaner, evenly spaced layout: the sections run down the left, and the options sit in an even grid on the right. Before, half the window was empty and the options were squeezed into one column.
  • The search box, Redo car and Done sit in one tidy bar. Selected options have a teal outline and dot, and the five-step road bars are teal to match.
  • On phones held sideways, settings fill the screen with a narrower list of sections. Held upright, the sections become a row across the top.

Fixes

  • Traffic lights no longer flicker or show stripes. The lenses, lit lamps, backplates and their yellow borders no longer fight to be drawn at the same depth, at any distance.

Version 53 · Haptics

Haptics and vibration

  • Your phone now vibrates when you crash (harder the faster you hit), drop a wheel in a pothole, hit a kerb or a big bump, or drive over rumble strips (faster buzzes the faster you go).
  • ABS pulses through the phone when you brake hard enough to lock the wheels. Lane departure warnings shake like a real steering wheel. Forward collision warnings give a double pulse, and automatic emergency braking a long hard buzz.
  • Small taps for gear shifts and buttons, and the engine shakes when it cranks (EVs and hybrids give a soft tap).
  • New Haptics setting in Settings › Car: Off, Light (only the big moments) or Full. Full is the default on phones.
  • Works on Android phones. iPhone browsers only allow a tap when you touch a button; the App Store version would get full haptics.

Version 52 · Real suspension on AI cars

AI suspension

  • Traffic cars now use the same suspension as the cars you drive. Each one gets the suspension of its real model (coil springs, frequency-selective, adaptive, Magnetic Ride or air) with four corner springs and dampers, anti-roll bars and its real weight. Bumps and potholes hit each wheel separately, and soft air-sprung SUVs float while sporty cars stay flat.

Fixes

  • Cars waiting at lights no longer drift sideways or turn crooked. They don't start lane changes while stopped at a light, and they only move sideways while driving forward.

Version 51 · Realistic traffic lights

Traffic lights

  • New US-style signals: galvanised steel poles on base plates, tapered mast arms with a tie rod, and one signal head over each lane.
  • Each head has a black backplate with a yellow reflective border, round LED lenses and hoods over each lens, like real signals.
  • Left-turn lanes on bigger roads get a flashing yellow arrow head: a red arrow on red, a steady yellow arrow on yellow, and a flashing yellow arrow when you may turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic.
  • Every signal pole has a pedestrian signal and push button. It shows the white WALK person, then a flashing orange hand with a countdown that runs out as the light turns red, then a steady hand.

Version 50 · Traffic that reacts to you, AI suspension, new people

Traffic reacts to you

  • Honk at the car in front and it hurries up: it pulls away from a light faster and speeds up if it was dawdling.
  • Drive well under the limit with someone behind you and they flash their high beams. If there's a free lane, they go round you; aggressive drivers do it fast.
  • A new aggressive driver type (about 1 in 8 cars): short following gaps, quick acceleration, quick lane changes, and they honk.
  • Tailgate an aggressive or annoyed driver and they may brake-check you, so keep your distance.

AI cars have suspension

  • Traffic cars now dive when they brake, squat when they accelerate, lean in turns and bob over bumps and potholes. Lane changes ease in and out instead of snapping sideways.

Smooth turning

  • The steering wheel now eases in and out like a real hand, with no jerk when you start or stop turning. It follows the Pedal smoothing setting: Instant keeps the old direct feel.

New people

  • New, more detailed models for men, women and children, with real animations: walking, standing idle, and a proper seated pose for drivers and passengers.

Fixes

  • Grass no longer pokes through the road on hills, and junctions on hills now meet the road at the same height, so you can't fall through the ground there.
  • Parking lot lines no longer flicker.
  • Mobile: the start button now sits above the brake pedal, and the drive mode and terrain buttons sit above the steering arrows, out of the middle of the screen.

Version 49 · EV clusters, cruise screen, smarter traffic and people

Clusters

  • EVs without their own modelled cluster (Honda Prologue, Chevrolet and GMC EVs, Kia EVs, Audi e-tron, Jeep, Nissan, Subaru and more) now get the two-ring EV cluster from your photo: speed with the battery arc (0 to 100 %), power in kW with regen, tire pressures in the middle, READY, range, odometer, compass and outside temperature.
  • New adaptive cruise screen (from your Hyundai photo) on every car that doesn't have its real one modelled. It shows the road ahead, your car from behind, the car you're following with the gap bars, the set speed, the speed limit, and the green steering, lane and AUTO HOLD lamps.

Buttons and settings

  • The drive mode button is now square, with a TERRAIN button on top of it on cars with Multi-Terrain Select, X-MODE or Trail Mode. Hold the mode button for Crawl Control.
  • Road condition settings are compact five-step bars.
  • New Pedal smoothing setting (Instant, Natural or Smooth): the pedals move like a real foot instead of jumping to full. New Smooth stops setting (on by default) eases off the brake in the last metre so you stop without a jolt.

Matrix headlights, as in the US

  • Glare-free matrix high beams are only on the cars where the shading really works in the US as of October 2026: every Tesla, the 2027 Audi Q9 and the 2027 Volvo EX60. Other cars with matrix hardware (Audi, Lexus BladeScan, Lincoln, GM, Volvo EX90) only have auto high beams here, as they do in the US.

Smarter traffic

  • Cars no longer drive into each other inside junctions. If two paths cross, whoever gets there second waits.
  • Freeway merges work like a zipper. Two cars no longer turn into the same one-lane ramp at once.
  • Left turns take a real gap (about 4.5 s). Opposite left-turners go together instead of blocking each other forever.
  • Each driver has their own acceleration and braking (calm, normal or brisk), and moves into the right lane early for ramps.
  • Ramps now meet the cross street at a right angle.
  • In a 5-minute test with 170 cars, cars running into each other went from 57 times to about 5, and cars stuck for over 30 seconds from 15 to 2.

Smarter people

  • Pedestrians keep right when they meet, pass slower walkers, and stop for you.
  • On a crosswalk they wait if a car is about to hit them and hurry when one is coming.
  • Shoppers walk between the parked cars and the store doors, some pushing carts.

Fixes

  • Hybrids no longer show the old power-flow diagram in the panel under the red car. It goes straight to the new one.
  • Park assist works in the new parking lots. It finds a free bay while you roll down the aisle and backs in.
  • The roof rack and other accessories load in the background after start-up, so fitting them no longer makes the game stutter.

Version 48 · The new map

A real freeway

  • Hwy 7 is now a true freeway: no junctions, no U-turn crossovers. Four diamond interchanges (Woodward Ave north and south, Grand River Ave, Maple Blvd) with one-lane off-ramps and on-ramps that leave and join at a shallow angle, a gore and speed-change lane, green exit signs, and signals where the ramps meet the cross street.
  • The cross streets go over the freeway on bridges (girders, parapets, a pier line in the median, abutments) while the freeway dips into a shallow cut under them, with 5.8 m clearance. Lake Rd crosses on its own overpass.
  • AI traffic uses the ramps: it moves to the right lane early, exits, merges by finding a gap, and nobody brakes for cars on the bridge above them.

Outside the freeway

  • A ring of 50 mph county roads (County Rd 12, Ridge Rd) over new hills, bridges over the river.
  • Gravel roads: Quarry Rd, Gravel Pit Rd and Cemetery Rd, with ruts, washboard, potholes and loose grip. Narrow country lanes with no lines: Birch Hollow Ln and Mill Pond Ln.
  • Shopping strips on Grand River Ave and Maple Blvd: Fresh Market, HomeWorks, Bean & Brew, Burger Barn and Tread Center, plus two Fuel Stop gas stations.

Stores you can walk into

  • Get out and walk in: aisles stocked both sides, checkouts, produce, bakery, fridges, booths and counters. A button lets you buy things with your card.
  • Tread Center: drive into one of the three bays (or ask at the counter) to buy all-season, summer, winter or all-terrain tires, fix collision damage, or get an alignment.
  • Realistic lots: driveways cut through the kerb, 7 m aisles with arrows, back-to-back stall rows, islands with trees and lights, cart corrals, accessible bays, and EV fast chargers that really charge your car.

Your own house

  • Some houses in Rosedale and Birch Park have a red "For sale" sign. Walk up and claim one: the furniture moves in, and "Home" becomes a start point.
  • Every one has an attached garage and a wide driveway. Drive up and the garage door opens for you, then park inside.
  • The Fort St parking garage now has a proper driveway from the street with lane arrows and a clearance bar.

Roads you can feel

  • Settings › World › Road condition: choose how many potholes and how many bumps (None, Few, Normal, Rough or Destroyed). Bumps include frost heaves, sunken manholes, patched trenches and rough pavement.
  • New Proving ground (Go to › Proving ground): whoops, washboard, Belgian blocks, a pothole field, frost heaves, expansion joints, articulation humps, speed humps and tables, a curb drop, rough road, gravel, 10%, 20% and 30% hills, a skidpad and a brake strip. A message tells you what each section tests.
  • Green bike lanes with bike symbols on the collector streets and the new arterials, where cyclists ride. Benches and trash cans along the downtown sidewalks.

Version 47 · Real drive modes, terrain systems and suspension

Drive modes

  • All 107 trims of the newest cars (MKC, Lexus, Toyota, Subaru) now have their real drive modes, with the real names, in the order the button cycles them. For example: Lexus LX ECO / NORMAL / COMFORT / SPORT S / SPORT S+ / CUSTOM, Tundra ECO / NORMAL / SPORT / TOW/HAUL, Subaru SI-DRIVE Intelligent / Sport, Lexus RZ RANGE mode. The Outback and Ascent have no mode selector, like the real ones.
  • Each mode does what the real one does. Eco and Range soften the throttle (Range also caps power). Sport sharpens throttle and holds gears. Sport S+ and Comfort change the adaptive dampers. Snow softens take-off. Tow/Haul holds gears. Air suspension lowers in Sport. The description shows when you switch.
  • New round MODE button on the left, matching the start button on the right. Tap it to change modes. Hold it for the terrain system.

Terrain and off-road systems

  • Multi-Terrain Select (Auto, Dirt, Sand, Mud, Deep Snow, Rock), Subaru X-MODE (Snow/Dirt, Deep Snow/Mud) and Trail Mode change how much wheelspin traction control allows, and the throttle feel.
  • Crawl Control and Grip Control: 5 speeds, about 1 to 5 mph, feet off the pedals while you steer.
  • Downhill Assist Control / Hill Descent Control holds about 5 mph going downhill.
  • All of these are in the G radial and in Vehicle Settings › Drive Mode, only on cars that really have them.

Suspension

  • Each newest trim has its real suspension. Examples: FOX internal-bypass shocks on the TRD Pros, Old Man Emu on the 4Runner Trailhunter, Adaptive Variable Suspension and Active Height Control on the Lexus GX/LX, Lincoln Continuously Controlled Damping on the MKC Black Label. Adaptive dampers follow the drive mode, and it's shown in Vehicle Settings.

Version 46 · Hybrids like the real ones, Bluetooth audio, sitting fixed

Hybrids and plug-ins

  • Every hybrid and plug-in hybrid has the energy diagram (centre screen and the panel under the red car), including the F-150 PowerBoost, Grand Cherokee 4xe, Aviator Grand Touring and the Volvo T8s.
  • They drive like the real ones. Full hybrids move off and creep on electricity, the engine joins when you press harder or cruise at speed, and it shuts off when you lift, coast or stop. Toyota i-FORCE MAX trucks, the Lexus LX 700h and the Kia hybrids have one small motor in the gearbox, so their engine runs most of the time, the way the real ones do. Plug-ins stay electric until you floor them or the battery is down to its reserve.
  • Hybrid launch is fixed: the Prius now does 0–60 in about 7 s, like the real car.

Bluetooth audio

  • Tap Sources on the audio screen to pick FM radio, Bluetooth or USB, like in a real car. Bluetooth pairs your phone and plays its playlists.

People

  • You're the same person getting in and getting out.
  • Drivers and passengers sit on the real seat cushion, with knees up and feet on the floor, instead of sinking through it.

Older cars

  • Features an older car never had are gone from the car, the builder, the assist menu and the G radial. The 2011 SX4 has no driver assists. The 2019 MKC Standard has no adaptive cruise or lane centering, and no 2019 car has rear auto-braking or emergency lane keeping.
  • Fix: the real equipment from each car's build data now actually applies. Before, it was skipped when the game started.

Lincoln MKC

  • The MKC is now the full-detail model (about 150k triangles outside and 60k inside), so the body looks right again and the interior is smooth.
  • The gauge cluster is back as a working digital display, and the seatbelts are no longer red.

Version 45 · Lincoln MKC, 22 Toyota & Lexus, 8 Subaru

New cars (31 models, 107 trims)

  • 2019 Lincoln MKC (Standard, Select, Reserve, Black Label 2.3L).
  • Lexus GX, LX, NX, RZ, TX, UX and the new TZ. Toyota 4Runner, bZ, bZ Woodland, C-HR, Corolla Hatchback, Corolla Cross, Crown Signia, Grand Highlander, Highlander, Land Cruiser, Prius, Sequoia, Sienna, Tacoma and Tundra.
  • Subaru Impreza, Crosstrek, Forester, Outback, Ascent, Solterra, Trailseeker and Uncharted.
  • Each has its real trims, engines (turbo, hybrid, i-FORCE MAX, plug-in, EV), prices checked against the 2026–27 configurators, colours, and the builder's real packages, options, wheels and accessories. Toyota and Lexus get their own screens and clusters. Seats, driver position and centre screens were checked on every new car.

Fixes

  • The Ford and Lincoln reverse chime now plays on EVs and hybrids.
  • Reverse: the hybrid and EV reverse sound is a smooth whine (no more buzzing), and reverse power is limited like real cars (about 2–3 m/s² at most, topping out around 15 mph) for gas cars too.
  • Getting out of the car hides the driving HUD.
  • All people now use the new 3D bodies: drivers and passengers, people by broken-down cars, pedestrians, cyclists and you.
  • Features a car doesn't have are hidden instead of showing "Not equipped": in the settings menu, the Vehicle Settings page and the driver-assistance callouts.
  • Chrysler Pacifica third-row seats moved inside the car.

Version 44 · Driver assists tuned, new people everywhere

Emergency braking

  • AEB now sees people, deer and cyclists that are crossing your path (it predicts where they'll be when you get there), and brakes earlier for them. A jaywalker at 27 mph is now avoided every time.
  • Braking is modulated like the real systems: it brakes just hard enough to stop about 2 m short, instead of slamming to a stop 10 m back.
  • Clearer results: "stopped 2.0 m short of the car ahead", "slowed you from 57 to 20 mph", "braked for a pedestrian".

Lane keeping and hands-free

  • Lane keep assist steers back sooner, using time to line crossing like real systems. It now holds you within about 0.45 m of the centre instead of 0.8 m.
  • Automatic passing waits 5 s behind slower traffic instead of 10 before changing lanes.
  • Checked: adaptive cruise following, stop-and-go, cut-ins, hands-free lane centering, signal lane changes, evasive steering, blind spot assist, rear auto brake and all three park assist modes.

People

  • You and your passengers are now the new 3D people, sitting with hands on the wheel.
  • Cyclists ride the new 3D bicycle.

Version 43 · Phones, money, CarPlay and Android Auto

Phones

  • Pick an iPhone 17 Pro or a Galaxy S25 Ultra (Settings app). Lock screen, home screen with widgets, and apps that work: Northline Bank, Wallet, your car's app (lock, unlock, remote start, climate, horn), Maps, Music, Phone (Roadside Assistance really puts your car back on the road), Messages, Weather, Clock, Calendar, Garage and Settings.
  • Open it with Y in the car or P on foot, or the phone button on mobile.

Money

  • You start with $1,000. In the bank app you can take out a loan of up to $1 million (5k, 25k, 100k, 500k, $1M or any amount), choose 1 to 10 years, and see the APR and payment before you apply.
  • Payments are due every game week (7 in-game days). Interest is charged daily. Autopay pays from checking. Miss a payment and you get a late fee, your credit score drops, and new loans are declined until you catch up. There's a credit card with a limit that depends on your score, a minimum payment and a statement every week.
  • Fuel and charging now cost real money at real US prices: regular, premium or diesel depending on your car, and fast-charging per kWh. You pay with the debit or credit card you pick in Wallet. If there isn't enough money, the card is declined.
  • On the builder's last tab, pick how you'll pay: test drive (free), buy outright, finance (36–72 months, 0–20% down) or a 36-month lease. The rate depends on your credit score.

Apple CarPlay and Android Auto

  • Connect your phone (Settings app, the Bluetooth button or the screen's Phone Projection) and CarPlay (iPhone) or Android Auto (Samsung) takes over the centre screen. CarPlay has the dashboard with the map, now playing and suggestions, plus the app grid and status bar. Android Auto has the split screen, taskbar, launcher and voice button.
  • Like the real cars, Teslas and GM's newer EVs don't support CarPlay or Android Auto, only Bluetooth.

Screens and cameras

  • New Vehicle Settings page like Kia's: a list of categories (Driver Assistance, Drive Mode, Lights, Head-Up Display, Cluster, Sound, Seats & Comfort, Camera, Phone Projection, All Controls). Driver Assistance shows the car with tappable call-outs.
  • Tap the red car in the middle of the bottom bar to bring back the panel with the hybrid diagram, mpg and energy, lane-keeping and suspension views. Tap the panel to switch.
  • Guidance lines always show below 15 mph. Shifting into Drive shows the front camera on every car that has one. The Side camera button only appears on cars with a 360° camera.
  • Zoom into the cluster with N (or the 🔍 button on mobile). Volvo maps now fill the screen, are light like Google Maps, and have zoom buttons.

World

  • Day and night cycle: 1 hour in the game = 1 minute in real life. Sunrise, sunset colours, and headlights come on automatically at dusk. The Clock app can skip ahead.
  • New 3D accessories fitted to each car: roof rack, roof cargo box, kayak, bikes on the roof or on a hitch rack, tow hitch, window and hood deflectors.
  • Animated people, children, dogs on walks and deer, and you look like a real person when walking.
  • "Just walk around" at the top of the builder starts you on foot.

Sounds and mobile

  • Ford and Lincoln reverse chime is only on hybrids now and uses your original recording, looped. Gas cars don't make a reverse sound. Toyota and Lexus reverse beeps are only on hybrids and EVs.
  • Mobile: smaller buttons that fit an iPhone 17 Pro, you can press two things at once, and you don't need to hold the brake to start the car or shift out of Park.

Version 42 · Real builder for every car, accessories, more cars

Build & Price like the real websites

  • All 130 real models now have their maker's real packages, standalone options, wheel choices and dealer accessories, with prices, mostly from the 2026–27 configurators, window stickers and order guides (some prices are close estimates).
  • Packages and options really add their features: lane centering, hands-free driving, auto lane change, park assist, 360° / front camera, head-up display, matrix headlights, more power, sport exhaust, off-road grip and more. The Interior tab lists what's standard on your trim.
  • Accessories show up on the car: roof rails, cross bars, roof cargo box, roof and hitch bike racks, kayak, tow hitch, mud flaps, running boards and rock rails, window visors, hood deflector, light bar, bull bar, skid plate, fender flares, spare tire carrier, tow mirrors, spoiler, roof stripes, and for trucks the tonneau cover, bed rack, sport bar, bed liner and bed extender.

Comfort features

  • Press I (or the new ♨ button on mobile) for the comfort features your car has: heated and cooled seats (3 levels), heated wheel and rear seats, massage, ambient lighting in 5 colours (lights the cabin), power liftgate, roof shade, premium sound, remote start and more.

More cars

  • Spawn another car: Menu → Spawn → Spawn another car parks the one you're in and opens the builder. Keep up to 7 cars. Press T (or Switch car in the menu) to jump into the next one.
  • New full screen button at the top right.

Cameras

  • Side cameras now look backwards down the sides like mirrors, and update twice as often.
  • Fixed automatic park assist: the parking sensors no longer pop the camera up and fight with the park assist screen.

Version 41 · New cameras, Toyota, Lexus and Ford screens

Cameras

  • New camera screen like Ram and Toyota: Top View on the left, the big camera on the right and buttons for Rear, Front and Side. Side shows both mirror cameras looking down at the front wheels.
  • Shift from Reverse into Drive and it switches to the front camera, and it stays on until you pass 15 mph. Guidance lines show until 15 mph.
  • Fixed the centre screen flickering between pages.

Toyota, Lexus and Ford

  • New Toyota and Lexus screens: icon bar down the left, a dark map with teal roads, a compass, zoom and Recenter. Lexus has the round temperature dials along the bottom.
  • New clusters: Toyota with the ECO / POWER / CHARGE ring, Lexus with the hybrid bar, battery and fuel arcs and distance to empty, and the Ford digital cluster with the blue speedometer ring. Ford's screen has a SYNC 4 style bottom bar.
  • Ford warning chime added for Ford cars.

Other

  • The electric motor sound is much quieter and smoother, and so is the reverse whine.
  • R now resets your car like new (repaired, full tank or charge) on the nearest road.
  • In the interior view the money and level boxes fade so they don't cover the mirror.
  • From now on, when a new version comes out, everyone playing gets restarted onto it and their saved progress is reset.

Version 40 · Builder steps

Car builder

  • The main button now walks you through the builder: Next takes you from Choose your car to Color, Powertrain, Packages, Exterior, Interior and Accessories, and only the last tab has Start test drive. Back goes to the previous tab.
  • The tab bar no longer overlaps the list when you scroll. The start location and graphics choices are on the Accessories tab.

Version 39 · New controls, damage and car builder

New controls (PC)

  • F turns on accessory mode. Hold S (brake) and press F to start the engine. EVs and Teslas are on as soon as you get in. E and Q shift up and down. Shift or P sets the e-brake. B buckles the seatbelt.
  • W, S, A and D drive. Z and C are the turn signals and X the hazards. L is the headlights, J the high beams, K the fog lights and H the horn. V switches to the interior view.
  • G opens a radial menu to turn safety features on and off, and U toggles automatic emergency braking. Backslash turns on cruise control, and + and − change the set speed by 5. R puts your car back on the nearest road.

Damage

  • The crash detection and airbags are gone. Hits now dent and crumple the body where you hit, break headlights and taillights, bend wheels (the car pulls and shakes), and a hard front hit damages the radiator: it steams and loses power. Reset or a new car repairs it.

Car builder

  • Make it yours now has tabs like the brand websites: Color, Powertrain, Packages, Exterior, Interior and Accessories, with a running price.
  • Powertrain lets you pick other engines from the lineup and upgrade FWD or RWD to AWD or 4WD where the real car offers it, plus a tow axle ratio. Exterior and Interior add wheels, all-terrain tires, seats and more, and they change how the car drives.

New look

  • New HUD on PC and mobile, with money and levels. On mobile it has steering arrows, new pedals and a start button. The settings menu is restyled and has a search box.
  • The 360° button is gone: the camera screen now shows the top view next to the front or rear camera automatically.

Fixes

  • New electric motor and reverse whine sounds. The old car's sounds no longer keep playing after you spawn a new car.
  • Fixed the white dot on the Audi and Kia speedometers. AI cars no longer make random turns at lights.

Version 38 · Volvo portrait screens

Volvo

  • Every Volvo's centre screen now stands upright (portrait) at its real size: EX30 12.3-inch, EX90 and EX60 14.5-inch, XC90 11.2-inch, XC60, XC40, EX40 and V60 9-inch. The screen housing is reshaped to match.
  • Everything on the Volvo screen works: seat heating (three levels, both sides), fan speed, volume and mute, climate AUTO, the home and apps buttons, previous / play / next in the media card, and the search box (tap it, then tap where to go on the map).

Version 37 · Every trim, every option

Full trim lineups

  • The 96 newer cars now come in their real trim levels, about 320 in all: Silverado 1500 WT, Custom, LT, RST, Trail Boss, LTZ, High Country, ZR2 and the 3.0 Duramax; Ram 1500 Tradesman to Tungsten; Pilot Sport to Black Edition; Telluride LX to SX Prestige and the hybrid, and so on. There are 436 trims in the game.
  • Each trim has its own price, engine or motor (V6, V8, diesel, hybrid, plug-in hybrid or EV where the real one does), power, drive (FWD, AWD or 4x4), driver-assist level and equipment.

Options like the brand websites

  • In Make it yours, almost every car now has its brand's real option packages to tick, with prices. For example: Ford Co-Pilot360 Assist 2.0, BlueCruise and the Technology Package; Chevy Super Cruise, Technology Package and Max Trailering; Jeep and Ram Advanced Safety and Technology Groups; the Audi Driver Assistance Package and head-up display; Kia's Technology Package; Nissan's Premium Package; Toyota, Lexus, Lincoln and Volvo packs.
  • Packages really add their features to the car (lane centering, hands-free driving, 360° camera, park assist, head-up display), and the price updates.

Version 36 · New cars' seats and screens fixed

New cars

  • Seats: in most of the 96 new cars the front seats sat up against the dashboard. Every car's front seats are now slid back to a real driving position, and the rows behind moved only where they needed legroom. You now sit in the driver's seat, behind the wheel, instead of inside the seat.
  • Passengers and test dummies sit in each car's real seats, all rows.
  • Audi and Kia: the centre screen now shows the live screen instead of a fixed picture of a map.

Cameras and screens

  • Volvo: Park Assist Pilot now shows on the centre screen.
  • Front camera guide lines on the road, bending with the steering. The Lincoln front-camera pop-up now stays up for its 10 seconds instead of closing at once.
  • The head-up display no longer shows through when you lean in to look at the screen.

Version 35 · Brand screens, hands off the screen

Screens by brand

  • Chevrolet, Buick, GMC and Cadillac: Google built-in layout, with the app rail down the left and climate along the bottom.
  • Kia (Kia Connect), Jeep, Ram, Dodge and Chrysler (Uconnect 5), Audi (MMI), the new Fords (SYNC 4), Honda and Acura (Google built-in) and Nissan each get their own colours and highlights.

Inside view

  • Only your hands and wrists show on the wheel now, so they don't cover the screens.
  • Steering wheels are lowered to match the corrected seating position, so they don't block the gauges.

Version 34 · Real chimes, new phone and key fob, smoother

Real chimes

  • Each brand plays its own welcome chime when you start the car: Toyota, Lexus, Jeep, Chrysler and Ram (Stellantis), Dodge, Lincoln, Kia, and Nissan/Infiniti.
  • Lincoln: the real hard-warning chime for collision warnings and Super-Cruise-style takeovers, the soft-warning chime for hands-on-the-wheel reminders, and the non-critical chime for things like "press the brake".
  • Chevrolet, Buick, GMC and Cadillac: the real indicator click, collision-warning beeps, parking sensor beep, rear cross-traffic beeps, Super Cruise emergency alert, notification and general chimes.

New phone and key fob

  • The phone now looks like a phone: Dynamic Island, status bar, the car's own app with the car pictured, big Lock and Unlock buttons, remote start, climate, honk, trunk and panic tiles, and a home bar to close it.
  • The key fob is now a proper fob with the brand name, a key ring and real button icons, plus remote start.

Performance

  • Only the nearest few traffic and parked cars get the full model; the rest are drawn as simple shapes (even fewer in the camera and mirror views). Traffic sticks to a small set of models instead of every car you've browsed, and text on the screens is drawn faster.

Version 33 · 96 new cars

96 new cars, 6 new brands

  • Acura: ADX, Integra, MDX, RDX. Honda: Civic Sedan, Hatchback, Hybrids, Si and Type R, CR-V, CR-V Hybrid, CR-V e:FCEV (hydrogen), HR-V, Odyssey, Passport, Pilot, Prelude, Prologue, Ridgeline. Nissan: Armada, Frontier, Kicks, LEAF, Murano, Pathfinder, Rogue, Rogue Plug-In Hybrid, Sentra.
  • Chevrolet: Blazer, Blazer EV, Colorado, Equinox, Equinox EV, Express (cargo, passenger, cutaway), Silverado 1500, 2500 HD, 3500 HD dually and EV, Suburban, Tahoe, Trailblazer, Traverse, Trax. Buick: Enclave, Encore GX, Envision, Envista.
  • Ford: Bronco Sport, Expedition, Maverick Hybrid, Mustang Mach-E, Ranger, Super Duty, Transit and E-Transit.
  • Chrysler Pacifica, Dodge Durango, Jeep Cherokee, Compass, Gladiator, Grand Wagoneer, Recon and Wagoneer S, and Ram 1500, 1500 RHO, 1500 TRX, 2500, 3500 dually, 3500/4500/5500 chassis cab, ProMaster and ProMaster EV.
  • Audi: A6 allroad, Q3, Q4 e-tron and Sportback, Q6 e-tron and Sportback, Q7, Q8, Q9. Kia: Carnival Hybrid, EV3, EV6, EV9, K4 Hatchback, Niro EV, Niro Hybrid, Seltos, Sorento, Sportage Hybrid, Telluride.
  • Each is one representative trim with its real engine or motors, power, torque, gearbox, drive layout, weight, tank or battery size, fuel economy or range, price and standard driver-assist suite: Super Cruise, BlueCruise, ProPILOT Assist 2.1, Honda Sensing, Kia Highway Driving Assist and so on. Each brand gets its own paint colours and phone app.
  • They load only when you pick them, so the game doesn't take longer to start.

Removed

  • The chat button is gone.

Version 32 · Damage, knock-downs, breakdowns

Damage

  • Front, rear, left and right are tracked separately and get worse with each hit. A damaged front cuts engine power, and side damage makes the car pull to one side. Settings › Spawn › Reset car repairs it.
  • Hard hits fire the airbags and turn on the hazards. A very bad one disables the car.
  • Phone crash detection: after a serious crash your phone counts down from 10 to call emergency services. Tap "I'm OK" to cancel.

Knock things down

  • Street signs go over easily, light poles at about 18 mph, and trees only if you hit them hard (about 28 mph). They fall over in the direction you hit them, and you lose less speed than hitting something solid.

Broken-down cars

  • Cars broken down on the shoulder now have the bonnet up, hazards on, a warning cone behind them, and the driver standing beside the car.

Cameras and sounds

  • Only cars that really have a front camera (the ones with a 360° camera system) show the Front button. The Lincoln front-camera pop-up follows the same rule.
  • Toyota and Lexus: a cabin beep that repeats while you're in reverse.

Version 31 · Hybrid energy monitor, chat, park exit

New hybrid and plug-in hybrid energy monitor

  • Every hybrid and plug-in hybrid now has a Toyota-style energy monitor: the car from above with the engine, motor, battery and wheels, and moving arrows that show where the power goes. Orange is the engine, green is electric drive, blue is charging (braking, the engine charging the battery, or plugged in). Toyota and Lexus AWD hybrids also show the rear motor.
  • Read-outs underneath: battery level, EV range and drive mode on plug-ins, engine and motor kW, and trip mpg.
  • The same diagram is on the outside view too: tap the panel on the right (Sensors › Engine › Energy flow).

Chat

  • The game's owner gets a 💬 button at the top to message everyone playing. Players see the message and can reply, and only the owner sees the replies.

Park exit

  • Now works from straight-in parking lot bays and garage stalls, whether you backed in or drove in. It pulls out straight until the car is clear, then turns into the aisle toward your signal (left if you don't signal). It stops if there isn't room.

Inside the car

  • You can see your own hands on the wheel and your legs, and the inside view no longer sits too far back or too high (the Aviator was the worst).
  • EX30: removed the black panel that covered the centre screen. The EX30 has no driver display, so speed and gear stay on the strip at the top of the screen.

Sound

  • New turn-signal tick-tock, like a real relay.
  • Ford and Lincoln hybrids have a deeper, fuller reverse sound.
  • Hybrids get a soft thump when the engine starts up, and engines blip on downshifts.
  • Switching cars fully silences the last car, so its engine no longer carries over.

Controls and loads

  • Fuel and charge are now sliders in Settings › Controls.
  • Cargo boxes stay inside the car: one layer, sized to the car's width.
  • Mobile: the P R N D buttons react the moment you touch them, so you can shift while holding the brake (the Model 3 bug).

Version 30 · New screens, controls and loads

Volvo screens

  • Volvo's Google-based portrait screen: map with media and phone cards (XC40/60/90, V60), the EX90/EX60 "Good morning" home with the car and quick controls, and the EX30's top strip with speed, gear and range (it has no driver display), plus the apps row and climate bar.
  • Volvo camera page like the real one: Park Assist Pilot and Assisted Parking Exit buttons, rear camera over a top view with red cross-traffic zones, and Tire Track / Towbar / PAS / CTA buttons. The driver display shows a red warning triangle for cross traffic and collision warnings.

Other screens

  • Toyota and Lexus hybrids get Toyota's Energy Monitor (engine, motor and battery flow).
  • Reversing guide lines are now drawn on the ground and follow the steering, instead of standing up in the air.
  • Tesla camera page laid out like the car: big rear view with the left and right repeaters underneath.
  • Lincolns: shift from R or P into D and the front camera pops up for 10 seconds (closes above about 10 mph).
  • Cars with real needle gauges (SX4, Optima, Soul, Altima, RAV4 2019, Q5 2019, Savana) now have analog clusters with a mechanical odometer and no lane picture.
  • Gas cars lose the Energy page; MPG (now and average) is in the cluster.
  • Each brand's phone app on your phone (FordPass, Lincoln Way, Tesla, Volvo Cars, myGMC, myCadillac, myAudi, Toyota, Kia Access, MyNISSAN and more; the 2019 Optima uses UVO). Connect your phone and it shows on the car's screen.

Safety systems

  • Smarter AEB: it waits until a car really is in your path and works out how hard you'd need to brake, so it no longer jumps at cars that are pulling away or turning off. Warning first, then partial, then full braking.
  • Blind spot works by lane, so changing lanes no longer flags the car in the lane beyond.
  • Lane keep assist steps back while you steer and only nudges gently. Emergency lane keeping only acts when you haven't signalled.

Settings › Controls (new)

  • On-screen steering wheel instead of the slider (mobile).
  • Throttle and brake response: Gentle, Normal or Sharp.
  • Seat height and fore/aft.
  • Fuel or charge level, cargo in the back and test dummies in the seats (choose how many and how heavy). All of it adds real weight.

Builder

  • Concept cars (Infiniti QX55 concept, Aureon HX) are in their own Concept tab.

Version 29 · Smarter park assist

Park assist

  • Perpendicular parking now works in every stall: both decks and every level of the garage, and the new parking lots. It looks on both sides (signal to pick one), only offers a stall it can actually get into, and plans a path that keeps the whole car clear of walls, columns and parked cars.
  • If it ends up crooked or off-centre it pulls forward and backs in again, up to three times, and tells you how many adjustments it made. In tests it parked within 2° and 3 cm of the centre line every time, with no bumps.
  • It slows to a crawl when something is close behind, and the park screen shows the lot stalls as well as the garage.

Garage

  • The columns now stand in two lines down the middle of each deck instead of at the stall entrances, so every stall can be reached.

Watts to Freedom

  • The shake is now a smooth, low rumble on the outside camera only. The inside view and the screen stay steady.

Version 28 · Smarter traffic, big trucks fixed

Smarter AI traffic

  • Drivers have personalities: calm ones keep a longer gap and drive a little under the limit, brisk ones follow closer, go a little faster and change lanes more.
  • They let you in: signal toward a lane and the car just behind you there backs off to open a gap.
  • They see trouble early: a crash, cones or a stopped car with hazards ahead in their lane and they move over well before it instead of queueing up to it.
  • Move-over: they slow down passing a stopped car with its hazards on.

Fixes

  • Big trucks (Yukon, Sierra, Sierra HD, Sierra EV, Hummer) sometimes wouldn't move after you switched cars: traction control was keeping the last car's grip estimate. It now starts fresh every time you spawn, and never trusts less than about half the grip of a dry road unless it's snowing or you're off-road.

Version 27 · Launch control, more stations and lots, a new viaduct

Launch control

  • On the cars that have it: Tesla Drag Strip Mode (Model S / X Plaid) and Launch Mode (Model 3 / Y Performance), GMC Hummer EV Watts to Freedom, Cadillac Escalade-V and Audi SQ5 Launch Control. Pick the sport mode, hold the brake, floor it, wait for Ready, let go.
  • Each has its own animation on the centre screen: Tesla's battery-and-motor progress ring, a full-screen Watts to Freedom with lightning and the truck shaking, and a chequered-flag Launch Control screen. Your 0-60 time shows when you get there.

Around town

  • Four more gas stations with canopies, pumps, EV chargers and a shop (fuel and charging work at all of them), and four more parking lots with parked cars. They show on the car's map.
  • New train viaduct: a concrete deck on twin steel girders with parapets, carried by two-column piers with cap beams. No pier stands on a road, a kerb, a pavement or the river, and the train stays up the whole way round.
  • More than twice as many potholes.

Screens and controls

  • Smaller head-up display.
  • Checked all the new cars' dashboards: the steering wheel sits below the gauges and every screen sits on its panel.
  • Reset buttons: ↺ Redo car in the Settings header starts your car over in the builder; Settings › Spawn also has Reset car position.

Version 26 · Level crossings, open houses, all features in one place

Train

  • (Replaced in version 27 by the new viaduct.) On the west side the train ran on the ground and crossed the roads at two level crossings: flashing lights, a bell and gates that come down as it approaches. AI cars and FSD wait for it. It's still on the viaduct over the river and the divided roads, with gentle ramps between.
  • Stay off the tracks: the train will hit you.

Open houses

  • Twelve single-storey houses in Rosedale and Birch Park have their front door open: walk in to a living room (sofa, coffee table, rug, TV) and a kitchen with a dining table. Inside, the view switches to first person.

Features and safety

  • New Settings › Features: every driver aid and feature your car has, each with an on/off switch, including Evasive Steering Assist, which now stops straight away when you switch it off.
  • Rear Cross Traffic Alert on every car with blind spot monitoring: double chime and a red arrow on the camera when a car crosses behind you in reverse. Cars with rear automatic braking also brake for it.
  • Auto hold is off when you start.

Cars

  • Gas versions next to the hybrids on the trim cards: RAV4 Limited, Nautilus Black Label 2.0L Turbo, Aviator Black Label 3.0L twin-turbo, F-150 Platinum 3.5L EcoBoost, and XC60 / XC90 B5 or T8.
  • The outside camera now sits at the right distance and height for each car, from the Civic to the 3500 HD dually (double-tap resets it to that).

Updates

  • When a new version comes out, the game starts fresh: saved settings from the old version are cleared.

Version 25 · 30 new cars: Volvo, GMC and five more

Volvo (11)

  • 2026 EX30 Single Motor ($38,950, 268 hp) and Twin Motor Performance (422 hp), EX30 Cross Country, EX40 Single and Twin Motor, 2027 EX60 P6 and P10 (launch model, 369 / 503 hp), EX90 Single Motor (329 hp) and Twin Motor Performance (670 hp, lidar), V60 Cross Country, XC40, XC60, XC90 (B5 mild hybrids) and the XC60 / XC90 T8 plug-in hybrids (455 hp, Pure / Hybrid / Hold).

GMC (14)

Five more

  • 2024 Honda Civic Si (6-speed manual, 200 hp), 2019 Kia Optima LX and SX, 2023 Kia Soul LX and EX, 2021 Nissan Altima S, SV (ProPILOT Assist) and SR VC-Turbo, and a 2011 Suzuki SX4 Crossover AWD.

Loading

  • The new cars load when you pick one, so the game still starts fast on phones and older laptops.

Version 24 · Trim cards and factory packages

Building your car

  • Trims are now cards like the maker's site: name, starting price, and a green "Hybrid", "Hybrid Available" or "Plug-in Hybrid" badge.
  • When a trim comes as gas or hybrid, you pick the engine on the card: RAV4 XLE (2.5L or 2.5L Hybrid), Lexus RX (RX 350, 350h or 450h+), Nautilus Reserve (2.0L Turbo or Turbo Hybrid), Accord EX-L (1.5L Turbo or 2.0L Hybrid).

Packages that can't be combined switch each other off.

Version 23 · Suspension, potholes, Lincoln and Tesla screens

Suspension and potholes

  • Each trim has its real suspension: passive coil springs, Tesla frequency-selective dampers, adaptive dampers (Lincoln CCD, Lexus AVS, Audi drive select, Model 3 / Y Performance), Magnetic Ride Control and Air Ride on the Escalade, Quadra-Lift air on the Grand Cherokee 4xe, adaptive air on Model S / X, and Adaptive Suspension with Road Preview on the Aviator Grand Touring and Black Label.
  • Real potholes: more of them, deeper (5–11 cm), jagged, with a broken rim. You hear and feel the hit. Adaptive suspension firms up the corner, Road Preview spots the hole with the camera and softens it before the wheel drops in, and passive suspension takes the full hit.
  • Settings › Car shows which suspension your car has.

Lincoln screens (Aviator, Corsair)

  • SYNC 3 layout: home screen with map, audio and phone tiles; Audio with Sources, Direct Tune and presets; Phone, Apps and Settings; the bottom bar Audio · Phone · Nav · Apps · Settings.
  • Cameras: rear camera with guidelines next to the 360° view, with "Please check surroundings for safety."
  • New Lincoln instrument cluster: RPM and MPH dials on a blue background, compass, station, outside temperature, PRNDS, odometer, temperature and fuel gauges, miles to empty, and EV range on the plug-ins.
  • The Nautilus keeps its 48-inch panoramic display and its own touchscreen.

Hybrid power flow

  • New diagram for the plug-in and full hybrids (Grand Cherokee 4xe, Aviator Grand Touring and Black Label, Corsair Grand Touring, Escape Plug-In Hybrid, F-150 PowerBoost): engine, battery, motor, wheels and charge port, with live power flows for electric drive, engine + boost, regeneration, the engine charging the battery, and plugging in.

Tesla screens

  • New Tesla settings with the real menu: Controls, Pedals & Steering (Dynamics on 3 / Y), Suspension (S / X: ride height and damping), Charging, Autopilot, Locks, Lights, Display, Trips, Navigation, Safety, Service, Software and Upgrades.
  • New Tesla dock with the car button, temperature, climate (Auto, A/C, fan, Bioweapon Defense, Heat / Cool, Keep On, Camp) and the apps.
  • New Energy app: consumption graph, average Wh/mi, projected range and each motor's power (one, two or three motors).
  • Model S and X show the driving view on the instrument cluster, so the centre screen is full width.

Version 22 · Multiplayer, double-helix garage, Smart Summon

Multiplayer

  • Everyone playing drives in the same town: you see other players' cars (their model and paint) move, brake and signal in real time, and they show on your car's map as blue dots.
  • Other players' cars are solid. FSD, emergency braking and the AI traffic all react to them.

Parking garage

  • Rebuilt with a double-helix ramp tower in the middle: two ramps wind round one oval lane, a level apart, with flat landings onto the decks on both sides on every floor.
  • Ticket gates at the entrance: take a ticket as you drive in (button or wait at the arm), pay on the way out (free under 15 minutes, then $3 an hour, $25 if you lost the ticket). The arms are solid until they lift.
  • The 360 / top camera now works inside the garage.

Smart Summon

  • Backs straight out of a garage stall or a tight spot before it turns, picks the right way to turn, recovers when it gets stuck and plans again. Tested from the street, a lot, a driveway and a garage stall with no bumps.

Fixes

  • Building your car no longer jumps back to the top every time you tap something.
  • Door mirror glass now sits on each car's own mirror, measured from the car's shape.

Version 21 · Tesla Toybox, smarter FSD, real mirrors

Full Self-Driving

  • Goes around crashes, stopped cars, cones and road work: it moves to a free lane next to it, or on a two-way road waits for a gap and passes in the oncoming lane at low speed, then moves back.
  • FSD profiles as in the real car: Sloth, Chill, Standard, Hurry and Mad Max.
  • Engage FSD from Park: it shifts to Drive, releases the parking brake and pulls away.

Tesla Toybox

  • New Toybox page on every Tesla screen.
  • Emissions Testing (a whoopee sound with the turn signal), Light Show (in Park, lights and music for 30 seconds), Romance Mode (a fireplace on the screen) and Rainbow Road (rainbow lane lines with Autosteer).
  • Speed Limit Mode (50, 65, 80 or 100 mph), Valet Mode (70 mph, Chill, Autopilot off), Joe Mode (quieter chimes) and Bioweapon Defense Mode on Model S, X and Y.

Mirrors

  • Real mirrors in the inside view: the door mirrors and the rear-view mirror show the road behind you. Switch to simple mirrors in Settings › Graphics on older devices.

Settings and players

  • Settings now has eight sections: Graphics, World, Car, Assists, Sound, Spawn, Tests and Log.
  • Everyone can now see how many players are online, next to the title in Settings.

Version 20 · New cars, park assist, plug-ins

New cars

  • 2026 Tesla Model S (AWD, Plaid) and Model X (AWD, Plaid), with Autopilot, FSD, the Tesla screens and the Tesla pedestrian sound.
  • 2026 Tesla Model 3: Standard, Long Range RWD and AWD, Performance.
  • 2025 Ford F-150 SuperCrew: XLT, Lariat V8, Tremor and Platinum PowerBoost (full hybrid: electric at low speed, motor boost, regenerative braking).
  • 2025 Ford Escape: Active, ST-Line Elite, Platinum Hybrid and Plug-In Hybrid.
  • 2025 Lincoln Corsair: Premiere, Reserve and Grand Touring plug-in with BlueCruise.
  • 2022 Lincoln Aviator: RWD, Reserve AWD, Grand Touring and Black Label Grand Touring plug-in hybrids.
  • 2024 Jeep Grand Cherokee: Laredo, Limited, Trailhawk 4xe and Summit Reserve 4xe.
  • 2019 Audi Q5: Premium, Premium Plus, Prestige and SQ5.
  • 2027 Infiniti QX55 Concept (a made-up future model): Sensory and Autograph with ProPILOT Assist 2.1.
  • The Jeep Wrangler has been taken out.

Choosing your car

  • A simpler builder in two steps: 1 Choose your car (pick a brand, then a model, then its trim) and 2 Make it yours (paint, wheels, tyres, options and the price). Start the drive and you appear at the place you chose.
  • Each model has its real paint colours with their names and prices.
  • Wheel finish: silver or black on every car again.
  • Tyres: All-season, Summer performance, Winter or All-terrain. Each has its own tread you can see on the car, and its own grip in the dry, wet, snow and on grass.

Plug-in hybrids and drive systems

  • Jeep 4xe and Lincoln Aviator Grand Touring are real plug-in hybrids: plug them in at the charger, 25 and 21 miles of electric range shown in the cluster and on the phone.
  • Jeep E-Selec: Hybrid, Electric and eSave, plus Max Regen. Lincoln: Normal, Pure EV and Preserve EV.
  • Jeep Selec-Terrain on the Grand Cherokee: Auto, Sport, Rock, Snow and Mud/Sand.
  • Grand Cherokee Active Driving Assist is hands-on, as in Jeep's press kit.

Park assist and Smart Summon

  • All-new park assist on the car's screen: Parallel park, Perpendicular park (garage stalls and charger bays) and Park exit. It searches as you creep along, then steers, shifts, accelerates and brakes into the space and ends in P.
  • Smarter Smart Summon: plans a route around buildings and parked cars, backs out when the way is behind, waits for people and cars, finds another way if blocked, and stops a few metres from you.
  • Parking sensors show on the car's centre screen, not over your view.

Start / stop, sounds and screens

  • Start / stop button (⏻, or I): gas cars crank with a real starter recording, hybrids and EVs chime READY.
  • A real dual-tone horn that sounds while you hold H.
  • Real recordings: Tesla pedestrian sound, Camry and Lexus RX reverse sounds, Ford and Lincoln reverse chime.
  • Sharper in-car screens on every car and setting, cameras at 480 × 288, off screens look like black glass.
  • Lincoln Nautilus: the 48-inch panoramic display is one continuous screen (gauges, map, clock, weather, media), and the touchscreen has Lincoln's layout with climate along the bottom.
  • Inside view fixed on several cars where the camera sat inside the seat; every car now shows the wheel, gauges and screen, and every steering wheel sits low enough that its rim stays below the whole gauge cluster.

On foot, accessories and options

  • Getting out: phone app and key fob instead of the car controls, Roblox-style walking, the car locks itself when you walk away. Your keys no longer turn the car's wheels and you don't hear the indicator outside.
  • Accessories fitted to each car: roof rack, mud guards, hood deflector, dashcam, head-up display (standard, option or not offered as on the real car).
  • Emergency braking sensitivity: Early, Normal or Late.

Screen and controls

  • The bottom bar is made for your car: its own names for cruise and lane centring (DRCC, TACC, BLUE, LTA…), and drive-mode, EV-mode and terrain buttons only on cars that have them.
  • Buttons for features a car doesn't have are gone everywhere.
  • Clean or full-info display is now in Settings › Car (shows the energy / sensor panel and the assist strip).
  • New settings sheet in five sections: Graphics (quality, weather, events, people), Cars (your car, its drive settings and assists), Spawn (where to go and the traffic), Tests and Log. On/off switches, above every other button.
  • Phones: built for landscape. If your phone stays upright you can tap Play upright anyway. Cleaner layout with less on screen, smaller phone app and controls.
  • The classic interface is back. Faster on older laptops and tablets like the Surface Go.

Around town

  • A train: an elevated line runs right round the map with a four-car train on it, and it sounds its horn now and then.

Version 18 · A living town

Real pedestrian warning sounds

  • The RAV4 Hybrid, Lexus RX hybrids and Accord Hybrid now play their real AVAS recordings below 20 mph, rising in pitch as you speed up. The RAV4 and Accord also play their reverse sound in R (the Accord's is the low Honda tone). Every other hybrid and EV keeps the synthesized sound for now

2026 Tesla Model Y

  • Standard, Long Range RWD, Long Range AWD and Performance, on your Model Y model. Autopilot is standard: Traffic-Aware Cruise and Autosteer with the steering-wheel reminder every ~30 s ("Apply slight turning force…"). Ignore it and Autosteer is off for the rest of the drive (shift to P to reset)
  • Full Self-Driving (Supervised): tick it when you build the car ($8,000), or buy or subscribe later on the centre screen under Upgrades, like in the real car. It drives itself: follows the route you set with Navigate on the map, picks the lane for each turn, stops for lights and stop signs and goes when it's clear, turns, yields to people and cyclists, passes slower cars and changes lanes (signalling first). Profiles: Chill, Standard, Hurry. No wheel nag with FSD; it watches you instead, so leaning into the screen too long gets "Pay attention to the road". Steer or brake to take over
  • Smart Summon (with FSD): get out, then tap Smart Summon and the car drives to you at walking pace, stopping for anything in front
  • The FSD visualization takes the left of the centre screen and the sensor panel: lanes, cars, people, bikes, cones, traffic lights and stop signs, and the blue path FSD plans. Also Autopark with FSD, Hold / Roll / Creep stopping modes, Chill / Standard / Track acceleration, Sentry, Dog and Camp Mode, Acceleration Boost on the Long Range AWD, and Premium Connectivity live traffic on the map
  • The driver-aid view in the gauge cluster was mirrored left to right: fixed
  • Lincoln Nautilus: the dash displays no longer poke through the windshield

2025 Lincoln Nautilus

  • Four trims on your model: Premiere and Reserve (2.0 L turbo, 250 hp, 8-speed), Reserve Hybrid and Black Label Hybrid (310 hp). All AWD with Co-Pilot360; Reserve adds Active Park Assist 2.0 and the 360° camera, Black Label adds BlueCruise hands-free on Hwy 7. AI traffic drives Nautiluses too
  • Emergency lane keeping is now blind spot assist: it only steers you back when you signal or drift toward a car in your blind spot. Leaving your lane otherwise just gets the normal lane keep nudge
  • H is the horn
  • Steering wheels sit closer and lower, worked out for each model so the whole gauge cluster shows over the rim
  • Grass no longer pokes through the road on Hwy 7

Fixes and realism

  • The gauge cluster now shows what every driver aid is doing: your lane and the lines around it (green or blue for hands-on or hands-free driving, amber when lane keep nudges you, red for emergency lane keeping), the car ahead and your cruise gap, cars in your blind spots, pedestrians, cones and deer, plus a status line (auto brake, lane keeping, changing lanes, stop sign…)
  • Stop signs are recognised: a stop sign shows in the HUD and the cluster, you get a warning if you come in too fast, rolling through is logged, and adaptive cruise and hands-free driving stop at the line and wait until you press Go
  • Hands-free lane changes take their time: the signal blinks about 3 s before the car moves, it only passes after following a slower car for about 10 s, and it moves back right after 15 to 20 s. AI drivers signal longer too
  • Rear camera guidelines now bend the right way
  • Bending headlights swivel only from walking pace up to about 50 mph, like the real ones
  • Parking sensors stop beeping once you are in P
  • Steering wheels sit a little lower so you can see the gauges from the driver's seat
  • Drivers and passengers sit properly in the seats, with their hands on the wheel. Pedestrians have jointed legs and arms with a real walking stride, rounder heads, longer or shorter hair, skirts, bags and more varied clothes
  • The camera no longer jumps around while you walk

New assist bar

  • A row of buttons across the top turns each driver aid on or off with one tap: emergency braking, lane keep, blind spot, emergency lane keeping, evasive steering, speed-limit assist (shows the current limit), auto high beam, parking sensors and auto hold. A button lights amber or red while that aid is acting, and is greyed out if the real car doesn't have it. On a keyboard, K toggles lane keep and N blind spot

Bridges, hills and a parking garage (part 2)

  • The Rouge River runs north to south through town with five bridges: Maple Blvd, Hwy 7 (twice) and Oak St (twice). They have parapets you can hit and the river below
  • Steep roads: Lake Rd climbs over a 26 m hill and Oak St over a 24 m one, with grades up to about 16%. Slopes now pull the car downhill, so hills slow you and auto hold matters
  • A 4-level parking garage on Fort St with scissor ramps, pillars, lights and parked cars. The camera stays low inside

People, weather and surprises (part 3)

  • Pedestrians walk the sidewalks, turn corners and cross at crosswalks on the walk signal. AI cars wait for them, and emergency braking stops for them too
  • Cyclists ride at the edge of the side streets and stop at lights and stop signs; cars pass them
  • People in the cars: every nearby car has a driver, some have a passenger, and you can see yourself in the chase view
  • Weather: clear, rain, snow or fog, changing by itself every few minutes (or pick one in ☰ › Car). Rain wets the road, snow covers it, fog cuts how far you can see, and traffic slows down for it
  • Random events: a crash ahead (traffic merges round it), a breakdown on the shoulder, road work closing a lane, a deer on the rural roads, someone jaywalking downtown, or the car ahead braking hard. Crashes and road work show on the map. Set how often in ☰ › Car
  • Get out to refuel or charge: stop at the plaza and shift to P, then tap Get out (or press U) and walk to the pump or charger. Tap Fill up or Plug in, then walk back to the door and tap Get in
  • New start points: Parking garage, Lake Rd hill and Rouge River. New tests: pedestrian and deer emergency braking, crash ahead, road work

Version 17 · New map

A whole new road network (part 1 of 3)

  • About 41 km of road, and you can drive every street. Your driver aids work on all of them: cruise, lane keeping, emergency lane keeping, blind spot, sign recognition and park assist read whichever road you are on
  • Downtown: a 6 by 5 grid of blocks with traffic lights on the busy streets, all-way stop signs on the quiet corners, crosswalks and parking on both sides. Parallel parking is on Main St
  • Maple Blvd and Woodward Ave: wide boulevards with Michigan lefts. There are no left turns at the lights: go straight, U-turn through the median crossover, then turn right
  • Rosedale and Birch Park: two subdivisions with houses, stop signs on every corner and speed humps
  • Hwy 7: a 10 km, 65 mph divided loop around everything, 3 lanes each way. Side roads join right-in, right-out, and median U-turns let you head the other way. The service plaza is on the north side
  • AI cars now drive the whole network: they signal and turn, stop at red lights and stop signs, take turns at all-way stops, wait for a gap, and yield before a left turn or U-turn
  • The red-light warning on screen is gone. Cruise still stops for red lights by itself
  • New start points: Downtown, Maple Blvd, Rosedale, Hwy 7 and the service plaza. Next: bridges, steep hills and a parking garage, then weather, pedestrians, cyclists and getting out to refuel

Smoother on slower devices

  • The page now loads in stages: a loading screen, then only the car you are looking at, then the other cars one at a time in the background while you pick (a small "Loading cars" counter shows progress). AI traffic adds each model as it arrives
  • New Graphics setting on the start screen and in ☰ › Car: Auto, Low, Medium or High. Low renders at a lower resolution, runs 12 cars, drops trees and shadows, and uses lighter physics. Auto picks for your device and lowers the resolution by itself if the frame rate drops

PC mode

  • Keys now: P parking brake, O hands-free, Q/E shifting, Z/C signals, X hazards. H, Space and 1-4 no longer do anything
  • Keys: Z left signal, C right signal, X hazards, Q/E shift through P R N D, V camera, R cruise, J crab walk
  • On a computer (mouse or trackpad, no touchscreen) the touch wheel and pedals are replaced by keyboard driving with small steer / go / brake bars; touching the screen switches back to phone controls
  • Keyboard: WASD or arrows, Space brake, Shift for gentle throttle, 1-4 for P R N D, plus shortcut keys for everything (press ? for the list), Tab menu, F full screen, M lean in to the screen. Steering eases off at speed so it is controllable
  • Gamepads work: analog steering and triggers, buttons for cruise, parking brake, camera, signals
  • On PC there is more traffic and the full-detail car models show further away

Regular Escalade and bigger concept wheels

  • The Escalade Premium Luxury and Sport Platinum now use your regular Escalade model (chrome grille and wheels); the Escalade-V keeps its own
  • Rims that stopped short of the tyre (on the Aureon HX and the Escalades) are now sized to meet the tyre bead

2026 Lexus RX and Cadillac Escalade

  • Lexus RX 350 (2.4 L turbo, 275 hp), RX 350h hybrid (246 hp), RX 450h+ plug-in (304 hp, about 37 miles electric) and RX 500h F SPORT Performance (366 hp, DIRECT4 AWD and Dynamic Rear Steering up to 4°). Lexus Safety System+ 3.0, with the Adaptive High-beam System and Advanced Park on the 450h+ and 500h
  • Cadillac Escalade Sport Platinum (6.2 L V8, 420 hp) and Escalade-V (supercharged 6.2 L V8, 682 hp, 10-speed, about 4.4 s to 60). Both have Super Cruise hands-free with automatic lane changes on the highway, air ride and Automatic Parking Assist
  • New V8 engine sound: the cross-plane V8's uneven burble and a deep exhaust, plus the Escalade-V's supercharger whine that rises with revs and load

Version 15

New line-up: 22 trims across 5 models

  • The Strata is gone. Pick from the 2025 Camry (LE, SE, XLE AWD, XSE AWD), 2019 RAV4 (Hybrid LE, XLE, XSE, Limited, plus gas XLE and Adventure), 2026 Explorer (Active, ST-Line, Tremor, Platinum, ST), 2022 Honda Accord (LX and EX-L 1.5T with a CVT, Sport and Touring 2.0T with the 10-speed, Hybrid) and the Aureon HX concept
  • Each trim has its real drivetrain, power, weight, fuel economy and equipment. Lower trims lose things the real car lacks: the Accord LX has no blind-spot system, the Camry LE and SE have Lane Tracing but no hands-free, only the Platinum and ST Explorers get BlueCruise and self-parking, the Tremor grips better off road
  • The Aureon HX concept (Hummer EV meets EQS) carries every feature we built: quad motors, 4-wheel steering, crab walk, matrix lights, hands-free Pilot with lane changes
  • All AI traffic is now a mix of these cars

Working screens and odometer

  • The centre screen keeps its shape on every car's display (it was squashed before)
  • The gauge cluster behind the wheel is now live: speedometer, tach or power meter, gear, fuel or battery with range, cruise and speed-limit sign, warning lights, and a working odometer and Trip A

Version 14

Real cars: 2025 Camry, 2019 RAV4, 2026 Explorer

  • Your three models are in the build screen with their real powertrains: Camry XSE AWD hybrid (232 hp), RAV4 Hybrid XSE (219 hp), Explorer Platinum 2.3 L EcoBoost (300 hp) and Explorer ST 3.0 L V6 (400 hp) with a 10-speed automatic
  • Each has only its real features: Toyota Safety Sense 3.0 on the Camry (Traffic Jam Assist hands-free up to 25 mph), Safety Sense 2.0 on the RAV4 (Lane Tracing Assist, hands on), and Co-Pilot360 with BlueCruise (hands-free on Hwy 7) and Active Park Assist on the Explorer. Things they don't have, like matrix lights or crab walk, are switched off. The Toyotas get EV mode and a B position
  • Their own interiors, dash screens and turning steering wheels from the inside view; the live centre screen sits on each car's real display. Their sizes, wheelbases and tyres set the handling and parking
  • AI traffic now includes Camrys, RAV4s and Explorers too

Version 13

P · R · N · D buttons

  • Four gear buttons next to the pedals. Park needs the car stopped, leaving Park needs your foot on the brake, and you can't flip between D and R while moving
  • Neutral really disconnects the drive: no creep, no regen, and in the gas cars you can rev the engine with Go (with the rev limiter)

Electronic parking brake

  • The (P) button in the dock. Stopped, it clamps the rear wheels. Pressed while moving, it does an emergency stop on all four wheels with ABS
  • It releases itself when you press Go in D or R, or tap it again with your foot on the brake. Shifting to Park sets it automatically. A red (P) light shows it's on

Realistic roads

  • Older grey asphalt in town and darker, newer asphalt on Hwy 7, with fine stones in the surface, polished wheel tracks in every lane, patches and sealed cracks
  • The highway has rumble strips on the shoulders that you feel and hear, and reflective markers on the lane lines that light up in your headlights

New tyre sound

  • A real rubber squeal that stutters and changes as you slide, rather than a tone, plus a separate scrub sound for wheelspin. Quieter on wet roads, almost silent on snow and grass

New electric motor sound

  • A soft motor hum that breathes, a faint gear whine at speed, and the inverter's stepped "sing" as you pull away, all quiet and louder only when you accelerate

Quieter wind and EV motor

  • The electric motor whine is now a soft tone at about a third of the old volume, and the pedestrian warning sound (AVAS) is much quieter, especially inside
  • Wind noise is lower outside, and from the interior view it is much quieter and muffled like a real cabin

Version 12

Gas Strata: 2.0T and 3.6 V6

  • A turbo 4-cylinder (260 hp) and a V6 (310 hp), both AWD with an 8-speed automatic that really shifts. It short-shifts when you're gentle, holds gears when you floor it, kicks down, creeps at idle and has engine braking. The tach and gear are in the cluster, and the panel shows mpg and fuel
  • Auto stop/start: the engine shuts off while you wait and restarts with the starter as you lift off the brake. The "A" light shows it

Auto hold (every trim)

  • Stop with the brake and let go: the car keeps holding until you press Go. The HOLD light shows when it's on

Regenerative braking levels (electric and hybrid)

  • Off, Low, Standard or One-pedal (lift off and it slows to a stop and holds). The power bar shows regen in green

New engine sound, and much quieter

  • Rebuilt from scratch: each engine plays its real firing orders, so the 4-cylinder, turbo 4 (with a soft whistle and blow-off) and V6 each sound different. Engine volume can be set to Quiet, Normal or Loud

Traffic sounds

  • The three nearest cars make quiet engine or EV whine and tyre sounds, panned left and right and with Doppler as they pass

Cleaner screen

  • A slimmer cluster with a power/tach bar, quieter telltales, one rounded dock for the buttons, and smaller pop-ups

Version 11

Real engine and exhaust sound (Hybrid and Plug-in)

  • Built from real 4-cylinder firing pulses, so it follows the rpm the way an engine does: muffler boom, intake roar, valve tick, a gravelly tone under load, and crackles when you lift off at high rpm
  • You hear the engine catch when it starts. It sounds muffled from inside and louder from the chase cam

Realistic TCS and ABS

  • TCS learns how much grip there is, holds each wheel at the best slip, brakes a spinning wheel on single-motor axles, and brings power back smoothly. The TCS light flashes while it works, and you can switch TCS off
  • ABS cycles each wheel through release, hold and reapply about 10 times a second, with the pump buzz and a pulsing brake pedal. The rear wheels share the lower pressure, like real cars
  • New road surfaces (Dry, Wet, Snow) and a "TCS & ABS on snow" test

Version 10

One big world

  • Downtown now connects to Hwy 7 with an on-ramp and an off-ramp, so you can drive one 8 km loop without switching maps
  • A more realistic downtown: towers with windows that light up at night, sidewalks, a park, street trees and lamps, zebra crossings, and signals for both directions
  • Hwy 7 has a concrete median barrier, guardrails, overhead green signs, farms and hills

Traffic sign recognition

  • The car reads speed-limit signs and shows the limit in the cluster. It warns you if you're speeding
  • Speed assist moves the cruise set speed to each new limit

Real collisions

  • Cars, parked cars, oncoming and cross traffic, poles, trees, buildings, the median barrier and guardrails all stop you, and the impact pushes both cars apart
  • Crashed cars stop and turn their hazard lights on. Cross traffic waits if something is blocking the intersection

Working centre screen

  • In the interior view, tap the screen: Map, Camera (rear view or 360°), Energy, Media with 3 radio stations, and Controls
  • The real dash buttons work too. "Screen" leans in so it's easier to tap

Fixes

  • Drag to look around now works on iPhone, and the view stays where you leave it while you're parked

Version 9

  • Build-your-car screen, park assist (parallel parking and pulling into a bay), gas and charging station, auto high beams, active headlights, new tyre sound, reworked lane keeping, and the grass-on-the-road fix
